newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia budget to confirm economic gains - govt.
newsitem.headline: Australia budget to confirm economic gains - govt.

text.p: Australia's 1997/98 budget will confirm the country's economic improvement over the past year and target the government's key consituencies when it is unveiled later on Tuesday, Treasurer Peter Costello said.
"This will be a responsible budget and it will confirm the economic progress we've made over the last year," Costello told reporters.
"It will also be directed towards our priorities for the coming year in relation to jobs and families and small business."
Costello is due to announce the budget for the fiscal year from July at 7.30 p.m. (0930 GMT).
Economists expect the government to cut spending by about A$2 billion to put finances back on track for a balanced underlying budget -- excluding windfalls such as asset sales -- in 1998/99.
Government forecasts, before any further cuts on Tuesday, project an underlying deficit of A$3.9 billion in 1997/98 and A$2.2 billion in 1998/99.
Economists expect Costello to announce an underlying A$1.9 billion deficit for 1997/98, down from the government's estimated A$8.5 billion underlying deficit for the year to June 30, 1997.
But some analysts have tipped a better result in 1996/97, fuelled by a stronger-than-expected economy, possibly helping the government to a small underlying surplus in 1998/99.
